local_articles.title: Karolina Muchova downs Naomi Osaka to set up Wimbledon semi-final with Coco Gauff
local_articles.snippet: LONDON – Karolina Muchova overcame four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka of Japan 7-6 (7-4), 6-4 in an absorbing contest of athleticism, shot variety and tight margins on July 7 to set up a Wimbledon semi-final against American Coco Gauff. The 29-year-old Czech, seeking a first Grand Slam title, proved the steadier player on a sizzling Court One, producing 21 unforced errors to Osaka’s 42 while the pair sent down 24 winners apiece. Not afraid to come to the net and volley, Muchova took the first set tiebreak with a forehand winner on her third set point. Osaka, 28 and seeded 14th, had downed top seed Aryna Sabalenka in the fourth round. But consistency deserted her as she served two double faults alongside two aces in the ninth game of the second set and missed a drive volley to drop her serve. questions.title: Which Chinese province will evacuate the most people in preparation for Typhoon Bavi by July 11, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Chinese authorities' figures in contemporaneous news coverage. Resolve to the Chinese province with the largest reported number of people evacuated in preparation for Typhoon Bavi as of July 11, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-11 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Broad multi-agency northward/northeastward convergence on July 6 reverses July 5's westward dip and strongly boosts Zhejiang's evacuation lead by the July 11 cutoff. As Cat 5 Super Typhoon Bavi (60-62 m/s, 895-915 hPa, 1000-1200 km circulation, 350 km gale radius expanding to 400-500 km) cleared Rota/Marianas on July 6, BOTH traditional NWP models shifted northeast toward the AI camp: ECMWF's afternoon run shifted from direct Yilan-Hualien landfall to grazing Taiwan's NE cape with its ensemble passing offshore north of Taiwan, US GFS similarly shifted offshore NE of Taiwan, while Google FNV3, GenCast, and EC-AIFS converge via Iriomote/Miyako toward Zhejiang (NOWnews 17:38, LTN, ETtoday 23:07). Taiwan CWA's 20:00 CST forecast shifted north (90% 120h gale hit in Keelung; forecaster Lai Hsin-kuo calls passing offshore NE of Taiwan most likely) and JMA targets Iriomote NW. Crucially, CMA's 17:59 CST July 6 briefing frames two mainland scenarios—brushing/hitting northern Taiwan then landing near the Zhejiang-Fujian border July 11 night-12 morning, OR curving east of Taiwan directly into Zhejiang—and Zhejiang Emergency Management already issued a July 6 province-wide directive warning of saturated Meiyu soils and full reservoirs to prepare for a worst-case direct super typhoon landfall (CNR). Across direct Zhejiang, Zhe-Min border, and offshore East China Sea tracks, Zhejiang's coastal/hillside evacuations by July 11 strongly dominate, lifting Zhejiang +0.095 (0.51 -> 0.605), cutting Fujian -0.090 (0.36 -> 0.27, retaining strong weight on western ensemble/Zhe-Min border scenarios), nudging Shanghai 0.055 -> 0.065 (Shanghai Met flagged severe Xiangshan-Wenling/northward risk), cutting Guangdong 0.04 -> 0.025, and holding Jiangsu at 0.025 (1% residual).

questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Synchronized July 6 northward/northeastward shift across CMA, CWA, JMA, ECMWF, GFS, and AI models flips Zhejiang back into #1 ahead of Fujian conditional on mainland China landfall. CMA's official 17:59 CST July 6 forecast explicitly narrows the primary mainland outcomes to (1) brushing or hitting northern Taiwan then making landfall near the Zhejiang-Fujian border (27.15N) July 11 night-12 morning, or (2) moving north east of Taiwan for a direct Zhejiang coast landfall (China Weather Network). Both ECMWF and GFS shifted northeast on July 6 afternoon from Taiwan landfall to grazing Taiwan's NE cape / passing offshore NE of Taiwan, joining JMA (via Iriomote NW toward Wenzhou/Taizhou) and AI models Google FNV3, GenCast, and EC-AIFS (via Iriomote/Miyako toward Zhejiang; NOWnews 17:38, CNA 18:22, ETtoday 23:07). However, because Q66613 is strictly conditional on a qualifying mainland landfall (void if Bavi recurves cleanly to Korea/Japan) and exact coastal geometry shows WNW-NW headings from Taiwan's NE cape (25.2N, 122E) still strike northern Fujian (Fuzhou/Ningde/Fuding) while western physical-model ensemble members retain ~17-21% direct Taiwan-landfall->Fujian risk (~95% mainland landfall rate vs ~70% for Miyako tracks), Fujian remains a close #2. Updating our 5-regime Bayesian landfall model raises Zhejiang +0.080 (0.38 -> 0.46), trims Fujian -0.045 (0.46 -> 0.415), holds Shanghai at 0.05, and trims Guangdong (0.055 -> 0.04) and Jiangsu (0.035 -> 0.025), leaving 0.010 residual for Shandong/Liaoning/other.
